QF.id: AIFM CIII Governance and Due Diligence_8

question.text: The Prime Brokerage (PB) Agreement with the Investment Manager of Chambal Managed Futures Fund (Cat III AIF) is being finalised. Which of the following is NOT typically a governance/operational-DD check performed by the manager on the PB arrangement?

answer.text: Rehypothecation limits and segregation of client assets
Margin methodology (SPAN, portfolio margin, TIMS) and intraday margin-call escalation
Asset custody chain-of-title and bankruptcy-remoteness in the PB's home jurisdiction
Allocation of Cat I/II co-investment PE deal-by-deal voting rights

explanation.text: The Logic: Operational DD on a PB covers: rehypothecation, segregation, margin methodology, intraday escalations, custody chain-of-title and bankruptcy-remoteness. Deal-by-deal voting-waterfall rights are a Cat I/II PE-IC mechanic unrelated to Cat III prime brokerage governance. The Trap: Deal-by-deal PE voting has nothing to do with PB operations. The other three options are canonical PB-DD items that a Cat III hedge fund CIO must sign off on. Cross-Exam Context: Cat I/II PE deal-by-deal mechanics are XIX-D territory (cross-exam context only for XIX-E). Cat III hedge funds almost never use deal-by-deal PE waterfalls. Manager's Pro-Tip: Insist on UCC-style 'segregation certificates' from your PB and run a quarterly bankruptcy-remoteness stress test — especially for global PBs where the Indian fund's assets may be booked in London/NY. A side-letter with a sub-custody override can save the fund if the PB enters resolution.
